text.p: TORONTO, Aug 6 Reuter) - The following are top headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-B.C. makes peace with Alcan: Court action ends as Clark pledges cheap electricity if job-rich smelter is built
-Reform proposes provincial wings: Party targets Saskatchewan
-At least 32 survive fiery 747 crash: KAL jet carrying 254 people goes down while trying to land at Guam airport
-Sex abuse blame pinned on Ottawa: Church urges apology to Indians
-The 'steel frame of India' showing a bit of rust: Bureaucrats in the elite administrative service run the country much the way the Raj that created them did.
-Big Three auto sales soar: July buying spree smashes records; scorching pace forecast to continue throughout year
-Ottawa lets Scotiabankj buy National Trustco: New parent plans to cut 500 to 700 jobs over three years
-Delrina alumnus back in business: Mark Skapinker took time off after he sold his stake to Symantec. A new profect has him eager to duplicate past success.
-Alcan, B.C. Premier both winners in Kemano deal: Firm cuts costs, Clark repairs image
-Alcan to build $1.2B smelter and end dispute with B.C.
-Scotiabank says 1,000 to go: Jobs will be lost over three years as Ottawa OKs National Trust deal
